title: Finite-field internal Hom finiteness over an arbitrary ground field
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $A$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, with its discrete topology. Regard $\underline A$ as a condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and let $A_X=p_X^*\underline A$ be its coefficient sheaf [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], equivalently the constant ring sheaf $A$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Let $P,Q$ be $A_X$-module complexes with cohomology vanishing outside finite intervals and with every cohomology sheaf constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on a finite constructible locally closed stratification each sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-values. Then the ambient derived internal Hom
$$
R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(P,Q)
$$
[sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] has cohomology vanishing outside a finite interval, with every cohomology sheaf constructible in this same finite constant local model sense. The ground field $k$ is not required to be finite, perfect or separably closed.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13 with coefficient ring R=A and ideal m=0, together with Definition 6.5.1 and Lemma 6.3.16; finite-type schemes over a field are quasi-excellent and ell is invertible. This is the finite-field coefficient specialization, not the integral assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence], $p_T^*\underline A\cong A_T$, and the exact module equivalence identifies finite constant local models. Finitely presented $A$-modules are the $A^d$, so a local model $A_U\otimes_AP$ is constant with value $P$, and finite constant values are free: this is stratumwise [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for bounded complexes with these constructible cohomology sheaves. [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison] identifies the statement's ambient Hom with ordinary ringed-site $R\mathcal Hom$.

The field $k$ is Noetherian, so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open subscheme remains Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. For a stratum factorization $S\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow g X$, the immersions are locally finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] and quasi-compact (closed subsets of quasi-compact opens; Noetherian open subsets). Thus $S,Z$ are again finite-type $k$-schemes, by combining finite algebra generators on affine charts. They are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Lemmas 6.7.11 and 6.7.13, geometric hypotheses on strata

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-stratified-generation] to $P$: it has a finite construction from $g_*j_!L$ by shifts and triangle extensions, with $L$ a finite local system on $S$. Fix $Q\in\mathcal B_A(X)$.

The two formulas of [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas] give $R\mathcal Hom(g_*j_!L,Q)\cong g_*Rj_*R\mathcal Hom(L,j^*Rg^!Q)$. Step 1's equivalence identifies $g_*$ and $j_!$ (compactifications with an identity factor) with the ordinary functors, hence by uniqueness their right adjoints $j^*,Rj_*,Rg^!$; so $Rg^!$ is that of [lem-sfb-finite-field-closed-support]. By [lem-sfb-finite-field-closed-support], $Rg^!Q\in\mathcal B_A(Z)$. Open restriction is the underlying abelian inverse image with its constant $A$-action; kernels and cokernels carry the induced action. It is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], commutes with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], and preserves the finite models by [lem-sfb-pullback-constant-model-constructible], so $j^*Rg^!Q\in\mathcal B_A(S)$. [lem-sfb-finite-field-lisse-internal-hom] handles the inner Hom, and [lem-sfb-finite-field-proetale-direct-image] applied to $j$ then $g$ puts the displayed value in $\mathcal B_A(X)$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], Hom into $Q$ sends first-variable triangles to triangles and shifts to opposite shifts. [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] closes $\mathcal B_A(X)$ under those operations. Induction over the finite construction in step 3, starting from zero and step 4, gives $R\mathcal Hom(P,Q)\in\mathcal B_A(X)$. Step 1 transfers both asserted properties back to the original module category. Empty $X$ and zero inputs give zero.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.7.13, proof, and Lemma 6.7.11; finite-coefficient specialization R=A, m=0, with finite stratified dévissage expanded using Lemmas 6.3.3 and 6.3.9.
